subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support `disabled` as a second MCP configuration key, or keep `enabled` as the only runtime contract and migrate legacy files through Doctor?
rationale: The branch changes public configuration semantics rather than only repairing an internal implementation: it validates a new alias, defines its precedence over `enabled`, and can persist the alias unchanged when false.

options.title: Keep one canonical setting
options.body: Reject `disabled` at runtime and add a narrow Doctor migration from legacy `disabled: true` to `enabled: false`, with conflict diagnostics.

options.title: Support the alias deliberately
options.body: Define precedence and conflict errors, canonicalize both boolean forms on every write, document the compatibility contract, and prove fresh-install plus upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical setting
recommendation.body: Reject `disabled` at runtime and add a narrow Doctor migration from legacy `disabled: true` to `enabled: false`, with conflict diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on schema and configuration-contract direction; available history links qiziAI to recent schema compatibility work, though direct MCP ownership is not proven.
